PM AutoTwin Studio
User Guide

This guide follows the actual product screens to show how to make heavy 3D files lighter and manage them as 3D assets, with originals, results, and records kept in one place.

As of November 2026 (v0.9.4) · Based on the web version; some screens and features differ in the installed version.
What you can do with this tool
  1. Make 3D lighter while keeping part names, hierarchy, and properties as much as possible, and export to the format you need (GLB, FBX, OpenUSD (Beta), and more).
  2. Start from a ratio recommended by file analysis, then change options and compare.
  3. Click an entry in History to return to that state. Nothing runs again, so no credits are used.
  4. Process multiple files at once with the same settings.
  5. Build a 3D asset library where optimized files stay together, with originals, results, versions, records, and comments in one place.

5-Minute Quick Start

For your first run, leave every option off and try the defaults.

  • 1. Open Opt on the left and drag a file into the center. On the web, you can upload up to 100MB per file.
  • 2. For a STEP or IGES file, the quality window opens. Start the conversion with Standard as is, then click Start Optimization in the Conversion Complete window.
  • 3. In the right panel, leave the AI Recommended Ratio as it is, set the output format to GLB, and click Run Optimization.
  • 4. Rotate the original and the result side by side, and check the vertices, polygons, and file size.
  • 5. If you are happy with the result, use Save to Asset to add it to the Hub library, or Download Asset to download it.
Tip

After you see the result, change one option at a time and compare. Earlier results stay in History, so you can go back at any time.

A Tour of the Screen

Left menu

  • Opt — Import and optimize assets.
  • Hub — A library that stores assets by project.
  • Viewer — Edit and measure scenes.
  • Gen — Create 3D with generative AI.
  • Setting — Manage your account, organizations, security, tessellation, and AI settings.

Changing the screen language

Click the globe icon at the top right and choose English, 한국어, or 日本語.

Navigating the 3D view

The controls are shown in the bar at the bottom of the screen. On the Opt screen, left-click rotates, right-click pans, the mouse wheel zooms in and out, and Z resets the view. Choose the center of rotation in Pivot Center.

STEP 1

Importing Assets

Open Opt from the left menu to see the file drop area in the center of the screen.

Opt start screen — file drop area and supported formats
  • Drag and drop — Drag a file onto the area, or click it to choose a file from your computer. On the web, you can upload up to 100MB per file.
  • Bottom bar buttons — The small bar at the bottom has three buttons. Import from Assets opens the Select Asset window, where you choose a project and search for files. Upload New File uploads a new file. Toggle Wireframe turns the wireframe view on and off.
  • Supported formats — FBX, OBJ, STL, GLB, PLY, STP/STEP, IGS/IGES, IFC(Beta), OpenUSD(Beta, shown as USD on screen)
Tip

If you are testing the same file several times, use Import from Assets in the bottom bar to reload the saved file instead of uploading it each time. It is faster.

1-1. CAD files (STEP/IGES) — choosing the tessellation quality

STEP and IGES files contain mathematical surface data rather than triangles (polygons). When you import one, a window opens automatically so you can decide how finely to divide the surfaces into triangles.

CAD conversion quality window — opens automatically when you import a STEP or IGES file · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)

Higher quality gives more accurate geometry, but increases the polygon count and file size. You can also reduce polygons in the next step, so choose based on the geometric accuracy you need now. Section 9 lists starting points by use.

  • Ultra Quality — Divides surfaces most finely. Intended for precision inspection, with the highest polygon count and largest file size. (Linear 0.01 / Angular 0.1)
  • Standard (default) — Offers a good balance of accuracy and file size, and suits most geometry reviews. (Linear 0.1 / Angular 0.1)
  • Lightweight — Loads quickly with fewer polygons. Curved surfaces may look slightly faceted. (Linear 0.5 / Angular 1)
  • Mobile — The lightest setting, intended for web and mobile previews. Surface distortion is noticeable. (Linear 1 / Angular 5)
  • Custom — Enter Linear and Angular values yourself.
  • Saved Presets — Save values matched to CAD tools you use often, such as SolidWorks, and reuse them.
  • Merge duplicate vertices (on by default) — Merges vertices at the same position, reducing the vertex count. Normals are lost as a result, so curved surfaces may look faceted. The geometry and polygon count stay the same.
  • Use these settings automatically for future CAD uploads — When on, later STEP and IGES files convert right away without this window. You can turn it off under Settings > Tessellation.

1-2. The conversion complete window

When conversion finishes, the Conversion Complete window shows the vertices, polygons, and file size, and you choose one of the following four options.

Conversion Complete — vertices, polygons, size, and four choices · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)
  • Save As Is — Saves the conversion result as it is.
  • Download Converted GLB — Downloads the conversion result as GLB.
  • Convert Again with Another Quality — Converts again at a different quality.
  • Start Optimization — Moves on to the optimization step.

To change the conversion quality later, click the Conversion Settings button at the top left of the Original view.

1-3. Importing OpenUSD(Beta) files

You can import a USD file you already have and make it lighter (Beta). Names, hierarchy, and instances are kept where possible, but results can vary by model. Part names in non-Latin scripts may be changed to Latin letters and numbers, so please check the result.

STEP 2

Running an Optimization and Options

Once an asset is imported, set up the optimization in the right panel and click Run Optimization. Check Estimated Cost before running. The value changes with your settings.

Optimization panel — before a file is added

When each option helps and when to be careful

OptionWhat it doesWorks well forBe careful when
AI Recommended RatioAnalyzes the file and recommends a reduction ratio.A starting point for first-time useThe value varies by file.
Reduction LevelThe ratio actually applied.Higher values make the file lighter.Mechanical parts may show faceted curved surfaces at 80% or above. Try starting at around 60%.
Optimization Goal: Quality PriorityReduces only as far as the geometry holds up.Parts where geometry matters, models with few verticesThe actual reduction may be lower than the set value, and processing may be slower.
Optimization Goal: Compression PriorityReduces to meet the target ratio.Web and mobile with a set file size targetThe geometry may distort. Seams have opened up in some scan meshes.
AI Vertex Importance Optimization (Beta)AI reduces polygons while preserving important vertices. Turn it on under Settings > AI Settings.Mechanical partsThe benefit is small for organic shapes such as characters and terrain, and processing takes longer.
Merge duplicate vertices (on by default)Merges vertices at the same position.When you want to reduce the vertex countNormals are lost, so curved surfaces may look faceted. The shape and polygon count stay the same.

The default for Optimization Goal depends on the input format. It is off for formats such as STEP, and on (Quality Priority) after analysis for USD inputs. Check its state before running. Optimization Goal is a Beta feature.

Optimization Goal turned on

STEP 3

Results and History

When the optimization finishes, the Optimization Results tab shows Total Time and the before and after changes in vertices, polygons, and file size. Buttons appear at the bottom right of the screen.

GLB result — before/after changes and download buttons · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)
  • Download Asset — Downloads the optimized file straight to your computer.
  • Save to Asset — If this button is shown, you can save the result to the library. You can load it again later or use it as the input for another optimization.
Files don't always get smaller

Because of how the FBX and OBJ formats work, a file can end up larger than the original even with fewer vertices. If file size matters, choose GLB, which is usually the smallest.

History — returning to an earlier state

The History tab adds a line for every run. Click an entry to return to the original, result, and settings from that run. Nothing runs again, so no credits are used. This is handy when comparing several settings.

Screen after returning from History · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)
STEP 4

Optimizing Selected Parts

The Hierarchy tab shows the part tree of the original file. Find names with Search objects, and select parts with the checkboxes.

You can reduce only the parts you select. For example, you can leave a large housing as it is and heavily reduce only the screws and bolts. If several parts share the same name, numbers such as _1 and _2 are added after the name.

Note

How the partial result appears on the results screen may vary by version, so please check the result.

STEP 5

Large Assets and Multiple Files

Choose one of three modes at the top of the screen.

Mode tabs
  • Single Asset — The default mode. Processes one asset directly in the browser.
  • Large Asset — A mode for working with large models.
  • Multiple Assets — Registers several assets at once and processes them in turn with the same settings.
Multiple Assets — processing queue, supported formats, and batch settings
  • Adding files — Add files with the + button at the top right of the queue. FBX, OBJ, STL, GLB, PLY, STP/STEP, IGS/IGES, IFC(Beta), and USD(Beta) are supported.
  • Batch settings — Applies Optimization Goal, the Target Reduction slider, and a preset equally to every asset in the queue. The presets are Plant Std (for plant equipment), Mobile (for mobile), and Balanced (for balance).
  • Min Vertex Count — A threshold that keeps small parts from being touched.
  • Start All — Runs the assets in the queue all at once. If a file fails during processing, it is skipped and the rest continue.
  • Job History — The number of completed jobs and the target ratio are shown on the right side of the screen.
STEP 6

PM Hub — From Optimized File to Asset

A 3D asset library where optimized files stay together, with originals, results, versions, records, and comments in one place.

Project and asset card · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)

Collecting assets

  • Projects — Collect assets by project. Use search, filters, and sorting, and view assets as cards or a list.
  • Asset cards — Show the thumbnail, vertices, polygons, file size, format, version, and download and view counts.
  • Copy, move, delete — Copy or move an asset to another project from the card menu.

Keeping the original and the optimized version together

Comparing the original and optimized versions, with per-file history · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)
  • Versions — v1.0(Original) and v2.0(Optimized) are saved together in one asset. Switch between them with the version selector at the top, and download each one.
  • Compare Mode — Opens the original and the optimized version side by side to compare the numbers and shapes.
  • Automatic tags — Tags are added when you optimize. You can also add your own.
  • History — Keeps a separate record of uploads, versions, downloads, views, and optimizations for each asset.
  • Scene Hierarchy — Search and check the asset's hierarchy and part names.

Working together

  • Comments — Leave comments on an asset and discuss them through replies. There is a feature for placing annotations on the 3D model to share comments along with their location.
  • Generate Secure Link — Creates a secure link to share. You can set how long the link stays valid. You cannot specify who (an organization or a person) receives it.
  • Invite Members — Invite colleagues to a project.

Adding information

Version selector, tags, and attributes · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)
  • Attributes — Attach text, table, and image information to an asset.
  • ERP/MES Data — New assets are filled with sample values automatically. It is not connected to external systems (ERP, MES) at this time.
STEP 7

Viewer — Scene Editing, Measurement, and Data

Scene, transform tools, Hierarchy, and Inspector · 3D model: AmazingHand by Pollen Robotics (CC BY 4.0)
Measure, view, and Data tools
  • Scenes — Gather several assets into one scene and save it. Ctrl+S saves, Ctrl+Z undoes, and Ctrl+Y redoes.
  • Adding assets — Double-click an asset in the list at the bottom to add it to the scene.
  • Transform — Move W, Rotate E, Scale R. Choose local or world coordinates, and add basic shapes.
  • Measure — A measurement feature for selecting faces, edges, centers, and vertices.
  • View — Change between Shaded, Wireframe, and Blend, and change the line color and camera.
  • Hierarchy · Inspector — Check the position, rotation, scale, and properties of the selected object, and add custom properties.
  • Data — Exports to and imports from Excel.
    Excel Export: three sheets — Hierarchy (node tree), Custom Data (user properties per node), Material (RGB color per node; only nodes whose color was set and saved in the Viewer, and other material information such as textures is not included).
    Excel Import: Using the Node ID, you can change node names, user properties and colors, or add new properties and colors. You cannot change the tree structure or add or delete nodes. Deleting a row in Excel does not delete the existing values. Changes are applied only to the Viewer screen.
  • Controls — Right-click to look around, move with WASD, zoom with the wheel, and reset with Z. A guide is shown at the bottom left of the screen.
STEP 8

Gen — Generative AI Connection

Generative AI that creates 3D from images or text is connected on the same screen. You can carry the models you create through optimization and storage in Hub. Web only; not included in the installed version.

STEP 10

Settings and Account

Settings has five sections: Account Settings, Organizations, Security, Tessellation, and AI Settings.

Tessellation

Settings > Tessellation
  • Merge duplicate vertices — On by default.
  • Convert CAD uploads automatically — Off by default. When on, files are converted right away at the selected quality without opening the window.
  • Saved Presets — Add values with + Add Preset. Example: SolidWorks (Linear 0.1 / Angular 0.8)

AI Settings

Turn AI Vertex Importance Optimization (Beta) on and off. It is off by default. Depending on the model, the quality and actual reduction may differ from what you expect, and the added analysis step may make processing take longer than usual.

AI Settings

Account and credits

Click the account icon at the top right to see your plan, available Credits, and Storage. If you belong to more than one organization, switch in My Organization. You manage your profile in Account Settings.

Account Settings and the account menu (account details are hidden)

Common Sticking Points

A window appeared when I uploaded a STEP file.

CAD files contain surface data, so you need to set the accuracy first. Start the conversion with Standard as is, then click Start Optimization in the Conversion Complete window.

The result looks faceted.

Try lowering the Reduction Level to around 60%, or turn off Merge duplicate vertices and convert again.

My file got bigger after optimization.

Because of how the FBX and OBJ formats work, a file can end up larger than the original. If file size matters, try exporting to GLB.

My file is over 100MB.

On the web, you can upload files up to 100MB each. For larger files, please contact us and we will advise you on how to process them (for example, with the installed version).

My part names changed.

Parts with the same name get numbers such as _1 and _2. In USD(Beta), names in non-Latin scripts may be changed to Latin letters and numbers. If you need to keep the names, export to GLB or FBX and check the result.

I want to go back to an earlier result.

Click the entry in History. No credits are used.

I want to show this to a colleague.

In Hub, you can create a secure link or invite members. Leave feedback in Comments.

When are credits used?

Credits are used when you run an optimization, and Estimated Cost is shown before you run. Viewing History, Hub, and Viewer does not use credits.

Can I download as OpenUSD(Beta)? Does it work with IFC?

Yes. Choose USD(Beta) in Output Format. You can also import IFC(Beta) files.
